scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Depends on: Phase 0 (V0 passes)"; Phase 2 depends on V1, V1b pass; write scope only added after injection test
scores.rationale: Phases progress from read-only client to accuracy/injection validation to comments to closes, each gated on the prior proof.

scores.evidence: "Fetch one real open GitHub issue... call LLM... store result in a local trace file, and roll back"
scores.rationale: It is a real end-to-end slice, but it runs locally/laptop, read-only, with no production deployment path, so it is only partly a prod skeleton.

scores.evidence: "R3 (closes are irreversible...) | Default: Triage-only Phase 0–1... | Flip condition: if >10% of closes are reopened, revert to triage-only"
scores.rationale: The tradeoff table gives reversibility tiers, defaults, assumptions, validation and flip conditions for the key decisions.

scores.evidence: "Rework runs widest first (accuracy & injection in Phase 1 before responses/closes)"
scores.rationale: Some blast-radius ordering exists (read-only then comments then closes, one repo then many), but within-phase ordering is not explicit and Phase 4 hardening comes late.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 hardening: "None in Phase 0; runs on defaults (no retry, no budget ceiling, no injection test)."
scores.rationale: Security has per-phase entries in the cross-cutting table, but Phase 0 has thin security and contradictions between sanitization and "no injection test".

scores.evidence: "Trace file v0-*.jsonl logged per call: [issue_id, model, cost, latency, timestamp]" with metrics, dashboard, alerts, centralized logging in later phases
scores.rationale: Observability starts in Phase 0 and is extended concretely in every later phase.

scores.evidence: "Prompt template versioned in Git; model version fixed (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04)"; "train/test split deterministic (seed=42)"
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed concretely in each phase: prompts, models, data, templates, rules, config.
Resilience appears from Phase 1 onward, but Phase 0 has none and the real circuit breaker and retry hardening come late, with inconsistent fail-open versus fail-close.

scores.evidence: "prompt-injection / guardrail defense, cost + latency budget, and human-in-the-loop gating come FIRST, then retrieval → model access → memory → orchestration → routing → feedback."
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human gates precede capabilities, with model access next, N/A for retrieval, memory and routing with reasons, and feedback deferred.

scores.evidence: "Multi-model routing: Deferred to Phase 4+. Condition: if phase accuracy diverges by issue type, add classifier"
scores.rationale: Seven deferred items each have a stated pull-forward condition.

note: Strong gating, tradeoff tables and AI-layer ordering; weaknesses are a local-only skeleton, no Phase 0 resilience, and weak blast-radius ordering within phases.
